deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.1 夢 — Core Words
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第一章「夢」
notes: Everyday words (mostly N4–N3, plus common N2 words and set phrases) for Chapter 1. Study this deck first. In this edition Chapter 1 is just the prologue (pp.5–8), and every card here is checked against the printed pages; each card's scene gives its page. Words from your notebook are tagged flagged_in_notebook. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: p.5 — a familiar voice from the dream (懐かしい声).
cards.context: 声 is a voice (people, animals); 音 (おと) is a sound made by things. 声をかける = to speak to someone.
cards.example_sentence: 後ろから誰かの声が聞こえた。
cards.example_reading: うしろ から だれか の こえ が きこえた。
cards.example_meaning: I heard someone's voice behind me.

cards.scene: p.5 — someone precious (大切なだれか); on p.6 he senses something precious was once in his hand.
cards.context: な-adjective: 大切な人 (someone dear). Close to 大事; 大切 sounds a little warmer. 大切にする = to treasure, take good care of.
cards.example_sentence: これは祖母にもらった大切な時計だ。
cards.example_reading: これ は そぼ に もらった たいせつな とけい だ。
cards.example_meaning: This is a precious watch my grandmother gave me.

cards.scene: p.5 — she was close to someone precious, but who? On p.8 both of them are searching for someone.
cards.context: The book writes it in kana; kanji 誰か. 誰か = someone; 誰も〜ない = no one; 誰でも = anyone. Same pattern: 何か (something), どこか (somewhere). Searching for 'someone' without knowing who runs through the whole book.
cards.example_sentence: 誰かがドアをノックしている。
cards.example_reading: だれか が ドア を ノック して いる。
cards.example_meaning: Someone is knocking on the door.

cards.scene: p.5 — like back when we were nursing babies (乳飲み児の頃).
cards.context: 子どもの頃 = when I was a child. After a clock time it's usually read ごろ: 三時頃 (さんじごろ) = around three.
cards.example_sentence: 子どもの頃、よくこの川で泳いだ。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ、 よく この かわ で およいだ。
cards.example_meaning: When I was a child, I often swam in this river.

cards.scene: p.5 — in the dream there is no anxiety at all.
cards.context: 不 (not) + 安 (at ease). 不安になる / 不安がある / 不安な顔. Opposite: 安心 (あんしん). 心配 is worry about something specific; 不安 is a vaguer unease.
cards.example_sentence: 明日の試験のことを考えると、不安になる。
cards.example_reading: あした の しけん の こと を かんがえる と、 ふあん に なる。
cards.example_meaning: When I think about tomorrow's exam, I get anxious.

cards.scene: p.5 — no anxiety and no loneliness (寂しさ) at all.
cards.context: 寂しい (lonely) + さ → a noun (see the 〜さ grammar card). Also written 淋しい. 寂しくなる = to feel lonely, to miss someone.
cards.example_sentence: 一人暮らしを始めて、初めて寂しさを知った。
cards.example_reading: ひとりぐらし を はじめて、 はじめて さびしさ を しった。
cards.example_meaning: When I started living alone, I learned what loneliness was for the first time.

cards.scene: The chapter title 「夢」; on p.6 she realises she was dreaming (夢を見ていたんだ).
cards.context: 夢を見る = to have a dream (not 夢をする). 夢がかなう = a dream comes true; 夢中 (むちゅう) = absorbed in something.
cards.example_sentence: ゆうべ、空を飛ぶ夢を見た。
cards.example_reading: ゆうべ、 そら を とぶ ゆめ を みた。
cards.example_meaning: Last night I dreamed I was flying.

cards.scene: p.6 — on waking, tears spill before she can think; it happens to her sometimes.
cards.context: 涙が出る / 涙がこぼれる / 涙を流す. 涙ぐむ (なみだぐむ) = to tear up. 泣く is the verb 'to cry'.
cards.example_sentence: 映画の最後で、思わず涙が出た。
cards.example_reading: えいが の さいご で、 おもわず なみだ が でた。
cards.example_meaning: At the end of the film, tears came before I knew it.

cards.scene: p.6 — sometimes she wakes up in the morning and finds herself crying.
cards.context: 目が覚める = you wake up (eyes 'come awake'). 起きる = you get up. 目を覚ます = to wake (yourself or someone). 目覚まし時計 = alarm clock.
cards.example_sentence: 朝五時に目が覚めて、もう眠れなかった。
cards.example_reading: あさ ごじ に め が さめて、 もう ねむれなかった。
cards.example_meaning: I woke up at five in the morning and couldn't get back to sleep.

cards.scene: p.6 — she wakes up crying for no reason she can name.
cards.context: なぜ (why) + か → 'for some reason'. More casual equivalents: なんだか, 何となく.
cards.example_sentence: なぜか、その歌を聞くと胸が痛くなる。
cards.example_reading: なぜか、 その うた を きく と むね が いたく なる。
cards.example_meaning: For some reason, my chest aches when I hear that song.

cards.scene: p.6 — the warm feeling vanishes without a trace (跡形もなく). One of the words you flagged.
cards.context: 跡形 = marks or traces left behind. Almost always with a vanishing verb: 跡形もなく消える / なくなる = to vanish completely. Compare 跡地 (the site where something used to stand).
cards.example_sentence: 古い校舎は取り壊され、跡形もなく消えていた。
cards.example_reading: ふるい こうしゃ は とりこわされ、 あとかた も なく きえて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The old school building had been torn down and was gone without a trace.

cards.scene: p.6 — he can't work it out, so he gives up and gets out of bed.
cards.context: The book writes it in kana; kanji 諦める. Often written in kana (あきらめる); 諦 is a hard kanji. 〜を諦める = to give up on something. やめる just means to stop; 諦める means letting go of a hope.
cards.example_sentence: 雨が強くなったので、山に登るのを諦めた。
cards.example_reading: あめ が つよく なった ので、 やま に のぼる の を あきらめた。
cards.example_meaning: The rain got heavier, so we gave up on climbing the mountain.

cards.scene: p.6 — he stares into the mirror; on p.7 she does her hair in front of it.
cards.context: 鏡を見る; 鏡に映る (うつる) = to be reflected in a mirror; 手鏡 = hand mirror.
cards.example_sentence: 出かける前に、鏡で髪をチェックした。
cards.example_reading: でかける まえ に、 かがみ で かみ を チェック した。
cards.example_meaning: Before going out, I checked my hair in the mirror.

cards.scene: p.6 — in just two seconds (たった二秒ほど) the warm feeling is gone.
cards.context: Stresses how small a number is: たった一人 (just one person), たった今 (just this moment).
cards.example_sentence: たった五分で宿題が終わった。
cards.example_reading: たった ごふん で しゅくだい が おわった。
cards.example_meaning: I finished my homework in just five minutes.

cards.scene: p.6 — the warm feeling that had wrapped around her a moment ago.
cards.context: プレゼントを包む (wrap a present). Figurative: 光に包まれる (bathed in light), 謎に包まれる (shrouded in mystery).
cards.example_sentence: 母はお弁当をハンカチで包んでくれた。
cards.example_reading: はは は おべんとう を ハンカチ で つつんで くれた。
cards.example_meaning: My mother wrapped my lunch in a handkerchief for me.

cards.scene: p.6 — tears spill before she can even think (涙がこぼれる).
cards.context: 涙がこぼれる, 水がこぼれる; 笑みがこぼれる = a smile breaks out. Transitive: こぼす (to spill something).
cards.example_sentence: コップが倒れて、牛乳がこぼれた。
cards.example_reading: コップ が たおれて、 ぎゅうにゅう が こぼれた。
cards.example_meaning: The glass fell over and the milk spilled.

cards.scene: p.6 — he stares at his hand; later he stares into the mirror (じっと見る).
cards.context: じっと見る = to stare; じっとしている = to keep still. A favourite word in this book's narration.
cards.example_sentence: 猫が窓の外をじっと見ている。
cards.example_reading: ねこ が まど の そと を じっと みて いる。
cards.example_meaning: The cat is staring out of the window.

cards.scene: p.6 — a tiny drop (his tear) sitting on his index finger.
cards.context: 人 + 差す (point) + 指: the 'people-pointing finger'. The set: 親指, 人差し指, 中指, 薬指, 小指.
cards.example_sentence: 人差し指で、地図の上の駅を指した。
cards.example_reading: ひとさしゆび で、 ちず の うえ の えき を さした。
cards.example_meaning: I pointed to the station on the map with my index finger.

cards.scene: p.6 — the tear that dampened the corner of his eye for an instant.
cards.context: 一瞬で = in an instant; 一瞬だけ = just for a moment. 瞬 = blink (瞬き = a twinkle, in Ch.2).
cards.example_sentence: 一瞬、何が起きたのか分からなかった。
cards.example_reading: いっしゅん、 なに が おきた の か わからなかった。
cards.example_meaning: For a moment I didn't know what had happened.

cards.scene: p.6 — the dream and the tear have both already dried.
cards.context: 洗濯物が乾く (laundry dries). Careful: のどが渇く (thirsty) is also read かわく but uses 渇.
cards.example_sentence: 天気がいいので、洗濯物がすぐ乾いた。
cards.example_reading: てんき が いい ので、 せんたくもの が すぐ かわいた。
cards.example_meaning: The weather was nice, so the laundry dried quickly.

cards.scene: p.6 — he gets out of bed and heads to the washroom.
cards.context: The room with the washbasin. お手洗い / トイレ = toilet; 風呂場 = bath.
cards.example_sentence: 朝起きたら、まず洗面所で顔を洗う。
cards.example_reading: あさ おきたら、 まず せんめんじょ で かお を あらう。
cards.example_meaning: When I get up, the first thing I do is wash my face at the sink.

cards.scene: p.6 — he heads for the washroom.
cards.context: 〜に向かう = to head toward (駅に向かう). Also 'to face': 机に向かう = to sit down at one's desk.
cards.example_sentence: 授業が終わると、すぐ駅に向かった。
cards.example_reading: じゅぎょう が おわる と、 すぐ えき に むかった。
cards.example_meaning: As soon as class ended, I headed for the station.

cards.scene: p.6 — the lukewarmness and taste of the water (ぬるさ) feel strangely familiar.
cards.context: ぬるいお茶 = tea that's gone lukewarm. ぬるさ = lukewarmness (adjective + さ).
cards.example_sentence: お風呂がぬるくて、なかなか温まらない。
cards.example_reading: おふろ が ぬるくて、 なかなか あたたまらない。
cards.example_meaning: The bath is lukewarm, so I can't warm up.

cards.scene: p.7 — he ties the necktie he's finally got used to tying (ネクタイを締める).
cards.context: ネクタイを締める = to put on a tie; シートベルトを締める = to fasten a seatbelt. Don't mix it up with 閉める (しめる, to shut a door) — same sound, different kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 面接の朝、鏡の前でネクタイを締めた。
cards.example_reading: めんせつ の あさ、 かがみ の まえ で ネクタイ を しめた。
cards.example_meaning: On the morning of the interview, I tied my necktie in front of the mirror.

cards.scene: p.7 — a tie he's finally used to tying; a Tokyo she's finally used to seeing.
cards.context: ようやく = at last, after a long wait or effort — a slightly more written word than やっと. ついに has a stronger sense of 'in the end it came to this' (good or bad). The kanji 漸く is rare.
cards.example_sentence: 三時間待って、ようやく順番が来た。
cards.example_reading: さんじかん まって、 ようやく じゅんばん が きた。
cards.example_meaning: After waiting three hours, my turn finally came.

cards.scene: p.7 — she gazes into the mirror as she ties up her hair.
cards.context: 見る + つめる (to press close): to keep your eyes fixed on something. じっと見つめる is a common pairing. にらむ is an angry stare; 見つめる is steady, often tender or intense.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は、窓の外の雨をじっと見つめていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は、 まど の そと の あめ を じっと みつめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: She was gazing steadily at the rain outside the window.

meanings: right in front of one's eyes
cards.scene: p.7 — Tokyo's scenery spread out before her eyes.
cards.context: 目の前に現れる = to appear right in front of you; 目の前で = before your very eyes. Also 'just ahead in time': 試験が目の前だ = the exam is just around the corner.
cards.example_sentence: 目の前を、大きな犬が走っていった。
cards.example_reading: め の まえ を、 おおきな いぬ が はしって いった。
cards.example_meaning: A big dog ran past right in front of me.

cards.scene: p.7 — the Tokyo scenery she's finally used to; on p.8 it flows past the train window.
cards.context: 風景 is often a landscape as a picture or impression: 風景画 (landscape painting), 田舎の風景. 景色 (けしき) is the view in front of you right now: 窓からの景色.
cards.example_sentence: 窓から見える田舎の風景が、とてもきれいだった。
cards.example_reading: まど から みえる いなか の ふうけい が、 とても きれい だった。
cards.example_meaning: The countryside scenery outside the window was beautiful.

cards.scene: p.7 — Tokyo's scenery spreads out in front of her.
cards.context: 景色が広がる; うわさが広がる (a rumour spreads). Transitive: 広げる.
cards.example_sentence: 丘の上に立つと、青い海が目の前に広がった。
cards.example_reading: おか の うえ に たつ と、 あおい うみ が め の まえ に ひろがった。
cards.example_meaning: When I stood on the hill, the blue sea spread out before me.

cards.scene: p.7 — once, she learned the names of mountain peaks without trying; now she knows Tokyo skyscrapers.
cards.context: 自然 = nature; 自然に = naturally, by itself. 自然な = natural.
cards.example_sentence: 毎日聞いていたら、歌詞を自然に覚えてしまった。
cards.example_reading: まいにち きいて いたら、 かし を しぜん に おぼえて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Listening every day, I picked up the lyrics without trying.

cards.scene: p.7 — he goes through the crowded ticket gates (改札を抜ける).
cards.context: トンネルを抜ける, 人混みを抜ける. Other senses: 力が抜ける (strength drains), 歯が抜ける (a tooth falls out).
cards.example_sentence: 人混みを抜けて、やっと駅の外に出た。
cards.example_reading: ひとごみ を ぬけて、 やっと えき の そと に でた。
cards.example_meaning: I got through the crowd and finally made it out of the station.

cards.scene: p.8 — scenery flowing past; a city where a thousand trains flow.
cards.context: 川が流れる / 涙が流れる / 時間が流れる. Transitive: 流す (涙を流す, 音楽を流す). 流れ = a current or flow; 流れ星 = a shooting star.
cards.example_sentence: あの頃から、もう十年の月日が流れた。
cards.example_reading: あの ころ から、 もう じゅうねん の つきひ が ながれた。
cards.example_meaning: Ten years have already passed since those days.

cards.scene: p.8 — leaning on the train door, she gazes out at the scenery.
cards.context: 眺める = to look at something calmly for a while (a view, the sky, the sea). 見つめる = to stare hard at one thing; 見る is neutral. 眺め = a view (眺めがいい).
cards.example_sentence: 窓から、夕焼けの海をぼんやり眺めていた。
cards.example_reading: まど から、 ゆうやけ の うみ を ぼんやり ながめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: I was gazing absently at the sunset over the sea from the window.

cards.scene: p.8 — streets overflowing with people; the city they both keep gazing at.
cards.context: Both 街 and 町 are read まち. 町 = a town as a place where people live (Itomori is a 町); 街 = busy streets with shops and lights. 街角 (まちかど) = a street corner.
cards.example_sentence: 夜の街は、昼間とは違う顔を見せる。
cards.example_reading: よる の まち は、 ひるま と は ちがう かお を みせる。
cards.example_meaning: At night, the city shows a different face from the daytime.

cards.scene: p.8 — a hazy (ぼんやりとした) white spring sky.
cards.context: Two senses: (1) a person spacing out (ぼんやりする, ぼんやり眺める); (2) something blurry or dim (ぼんやり見える, ぼんやりと覚えている). Both fit a chapter about half-remembered feelings.
cards.example_sentence: 電車の窓に映る自分の顔を、ぼんやり見つめていた。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ の まど に うつる じぶん の かお を、 ぼんやり みつめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: I stared absently at my own face reflected in the train window.

cards.scene: p.8 — she rides a commuter train through Tokyo.
cards.context: 通勤 = commuting to work; 通学 = commuting to school. 通勤ラッシュ = rush hour.
cards.example_sentence: 毎朝、満員の通勤電車で会社に行く。
cards.example_reading: まいあさ、 まんいん の つうきんでんしゃ で かいしゃ に いく。
cards.example_meaning: Every morning I go to work on a packed commuter train.

cards.scene: p.8 — the streets are overflowing with people.
cards.context: 川が溢れる (a river floods); 〜で溢れる = to be packed with; 涙が溢れる = tears well over.
cards.example_sentence: 休日の駅前は、買い物客で溢れていた。
cards.example_reading: きゅうじつ の えきまえ は、 かいものきゃく で あふれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: On the holiday, the area in front of the station was overflowing with shoppers.

cards.scene: p.8 — trains carrying a thousand people each.
cards.context: 列車 = a train (formal, often long-distance: 夜行列車); 電車 = the everyday word for an electric train.
cards.example_sentence: 北へ向かう夜行列車に乗った。
cards.example_reading: きた へ むかう やこうれっしゃ に のった。
cards.example_meaning: I took an overnight train heading north.

cards.scene: On the cover: 新海誠・作 — written by 新海誠.
cards.context: In book credits 作 = the author and 絵 = the illustrator. 作品 (さくひん) = a work; 作る shares the kanji.
cards.example_sentence: この絵本は、作も絵も同じ人だ。
cards.example_reading: この えほん は、 さく も え も おなじ ひと だ。
cards.example_meaning: The story and the pictures in this picture book are by the same person.
